He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's Gaels]] and the [[UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball|UC Riverside Highlanders]]. ==Early life and career== Perry grew up in [[Seddon, Victoria]] and came from a tall family, although his height resulted in breaking 13 different bones. His level of insulin growth hormone was found to be twice that of a normal person's, and a brain scan revealed a tumour on his pituitary gland. A month later, the tumour was removed and found to be benign.{{cite news |title=NBA career beckons for Seddon teenager who overcame medical scare |url=https://www.9news.com.au/national/nba-career-beckons-for-seddon-teenager-who-overcame-medical-scare/3fcf23df-b6fc-483e-b671-e736c3dfe43e |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=9 News |date=20 August 2016}} Perry was a relative latecomer to basketball, though his height provided an advantage. He arrived at the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in 2013, and sustained knee and hand injuries.{{cite web |title=JOCK PERRY BIDING HIS TIME AFTER SIGNING WITH ST. MARY'S |url=https://australia.basketball/blog/2015/11/18/jock-perry-biding-his-time-after-signing-with-st-marys/ |website=Australia.basketball |access-date=15 August 2021 |date=18 November 2015}} Perry played against future [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]] teammate [[Jock Landale]] once as a teenager, helping to score an upset win.{{cite news |title=Two Australian Jocks with unique paths to Saint Mary's hoops |url=https://www.ktvu.com/news/two-australian-jocks-with-unique-paths-to-saint-marys-hoops |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=KTVU |date=20 January 2018}} In 2016, Perry signed with the [[Melbourne Tigers (NBL1 South)|Melbourne Tigers]] of the [[South East Australian Basketball League]]. He committed to play college basketball at Saint Mary's.{{cite news |last1=Ward |first1=Roy |title=Andrew Gaze's Melbourne Tigers look to their cubs and China as SEABL return looms |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/andrew-gazes-melbourne-tigers-look-to-their-cubs-and-china-as-seabl-return-looms-20160326-gnrise.html?js-chunk-not-found-refresh=true |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=26 March 2016}} ==College career== Perry redshirted his true freshman season. He played sparingly during his three seasons at Saint Mary's. As a junior, Perry averaged 3.3 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=NCAA DI Spotlight: Jock Perry |url=https://thecannonnetwork.com/ncaa-di-spotlight-jock-perry/ |website=The Cannon Network |access-date=15 August 2021 |date=20 June 2021}} Following the season, he transferred to [[UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball|UC Riverside]] as a graduate transfer.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Adds Pair of Impact Transfers for 20-21 Season |url=https://gohighlanders.com/news/2020/6/22/mens-basketball-adds-pair-of-valuble-transfers-for-20-21-season.aspx |website=[[UC Riverside Highlanders]] |access-date=15 August 2021 |date=22 June 2020}} On 1 December 2020, Perry scored a career-high 21 points in a 57–42 win against [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite news |last1=Alexander |first1=Jim |title=UC Riverside men knock off Washington |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2020/12/01/uc-riverside-men-knock-off-washington/ |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=[[The Press-Enterprise]] |date=1 December 2020}} In the semifinals of the Big West Tournament, he posted 16 points and a career-high 10 rebounds against [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball|UC Irvine]]. As a senior, Perry averaged 11.5 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. He was named Honorable Mention All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]].{{cite web |title=Perry Signs Professional Deal with NBL's Ballarat Miners |url=https://gohighlanders.com/news/2021/4/23/mens-basketball-perry-signs-professional-deal-with-nbls-ballarat-miners.aspx |website=[[UC Riverside Highlanders]] |access-date=15 August 2021 |date=23 April 2021}} ==Professional career== On 22 April 2021, Perry signed with the [[Ballarat Miners]] of the [[NBL1 South]].{{cite news |last1=Gliddon |first1=Greg |title=Former US College basketballer Jock Perry is out of quarantine and looking for a Miners debut this weekend |url=https://www.thecourier.com.au/story/7220947/seven-foot-jock-perry-joins-miners-should-play-this-weekend/ |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=[[The Courier (Ballarat)|The Courier]] |date=22 April 2021}} On 17 August, Perry signed with the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]] as a development player for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].{{Cite web|title=JackJumpers Complete Inaugural Roster|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-complete-inaugural-roster|website=NBL.com.au|date=17 August 2021|access-date=17 August 2021}} While playing for the Casey Cavaliers during the [[2022 NBL1 season]], Perry [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ruptured his ACL]]. He subsequently missed the [[2022–23 NBL season]], returning to play the last 14 games of the [[2023 NBL1 season]] with the [[Diamond Valley Eagles]].{{cite news |last=Pike |first=Chris |title=Big man Perry expecting big Magic run home |url=https://www.nbl1.com.au/news/big-man-perry-expecting-big-magic-run-home |access-date=5 June 2026 |work=nbl1.com.au |date=5 June 2026 |language=en}} Perry helped the Gujarat Stallions win the 2025 [[Indian National Basketball League]] (INBL) championship.{{cite news |title=InBL Pro U25: Gujarat Stallions Beat Punjab Warriors With Thrilling Comeback In Final |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/sports/others/inbl-pro-u25-gujarat-stallions-beat-punjab-warriors-with-thrilling-comeback-in-final |access-date=2 March 2025 |work=Outlook India |date=1 March 2025 |language=en}} Perry joined the Diamond Valley Eagles for the [[2025 NBL1 season|2025 NBL1 South season]].{{cite web |title=Jock Perry |url=https://nbl1.com.au/player-listing/jock-perry |website=nbl1.com.au |access-date=1 May 2025}} He was named NBL1 South All Second Team and was the league's leading rebounder with 13.26 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Stars Shine Bright at the NBL1 South 2025 Awards Night |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/stars-shine-bright-at-the-nbl1-south-2025-awards-night |access-date=16 August 2025 |work=nbl1.com.au |date=15 August 2025 |language=en}} In January 2026, Perry played 11 games for [[Jiaozuo Cultural Tourism]] in the [[National Basketball League (China)|Chinese NBL]].{{cite web |title=Jock Perry |url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Jock-Perry/275345 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=4 April 2026}} He joined the [[Mandurah Magic]] for the [[2026 NBL1 West season]].{{cite news |title=Mandurah Magic are extremely excited to announce the signing of Jock Perry for the 2026 Mitsubishi Motors NBL1 West season. |url=https://www.facebook.com/mandurahmagic/posts/pfbid02CrwvLsEP5RkZYXNz3My3x5R6LW2HrtzDnByA24BpAZWPue8EKVund2XjyTbUkbWTl |access-date=27 December 2025 |work=facebook.com/mandurahmagic |date=26 December 2025}} ==National team career== Perry has represented Australia in several international tournaments. He played for the U17 team in the 2013 FIBA Oceania Championships, averaging 2.7 points and 2 rebounds per game. Perry was selected as a reserve player in the 2015 FIBA Oceania U19 Championship.{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Australian U19 Men's Squad - Training Camp Roster |url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/australian-u19-mens-squad-training-camp-roster |website=Pickandroll.com.au |accessdate=15 August 2021 |date=1 October 2014}} In 2019, he helped Australia win bronze at the [[Basketball at the 2019 Summer Universiade|Summer Universiade]] in Italy.{{cite web |last1=Arsenis |first1=Damian |title=Australian rising stars named for 2019 World University Games in Italy |url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/australian-rising-stars-named-for-2019-world-university-games-in-italy |website=Pickandroll.com.au |accessdate=26 September 2020 |date=18 June 2019}} ==Career
